issue.title: Repurpose Productive week into a weekly steps summary
issue.description:
Repurpose the current "A productive week" gallery composition into a simple weekly steps/fitness summary while preserving the strong bar-chart composition.

Owner direction:

* Remove the existing productivity framing.
* Reinterpret the composition as a weekly steps summary.
* Keep the card visually simple and focused on one primary metric plus the 7-day bar visualization.

Remove:

* "A productive week" title
* "Your workspace, at a glance." subtitle
* "tasks completed" label

Primary metric:

* Use a realistic four-digit steps value to illustrate thousands of steps, for example around 8,000–9,000.
* The large number should use the semantic Heading typography role (type-heading) rather than Body typography.
* Keep the number visually prominent.

Supporting copy:

* Add a label such as "Average steps this week" or equivalent concise copy.
* Add a secondary comparison such as "+12.4% vs last week" or similar positive weekly delta.

Chart:

* Keep the seven-bar weekly chart structure.
* Reinterpret the bars as daily step counts.
* Preserve weekday labels M / T / W / T / F / S / S.
* Adjust bar heights/data so they feel plausible for the new steps context.
* Preserve token-driven chart colors and responsive behavior.

Design-system constraints:

* Keep all styling driven by Personal UI semantic tokens.
* Use Heading / Body / Mono roles appropriately.
* Preserve light/dark theme behavior.
* Do not hard-code arbitrary colors when semantic tokens exist.
* Do not introduce a new public component/resource solely for this composition.

Interaction:

* No new workflow behavior is needed.
* Preserve stable card geometry.
* Keep any existing lightweight hover/focus behavior if relevant.

Do not:

* change gallery ordering/layout;
* change shared chart primitives unless strictly necessary;
* add extra fitness widgets or secondary charts;
* add workflow-heavy interactions;
* change unrelated compositions.

Acceptance:

* The composition no longer uses the productivity/workspace framing.
* No title/subtitle remains above the primary metric.
* The large steps value is a realistic four-digit number and uses Heading typography.
* "tasks completed" is removed.
* Supporting copy communicates average weekly steps.
* A weekly percentage comparison is shown.
* The seven-bar chart reads as daily steps and keeps weekday labels.
* Light/dark/theme-token responsiveness remains intact.
* Card geometry remains stable and responsive.
* No accessibility or containment regression.
